description: A firm with a whale customer — one customer carries most of the revenue. Tests concentration reporting without slipping into causal language.

at_risk.definition: customers with 2+ lifetime visits whose last visit is 45-180 days before period end

ranked.pattern: Saturday is the busiest weekday by visit count, but Thursday customers tend to spend more per visit — SGD 145.00 against Saturday's SGD 98.00.

comparison.detail: revenue-per-visit on the busiest weekday (Saturday, SGD 98.00) against the most valuable weekday (Thursday, SGD 145.00), both drawn from the same reader

impact.reason: no incremental model: knowing which day is valuable does not say what more staffing or promotion on that day would add

action.what: Do not assume the busiest day is the most valuable one — check whether Thursday's staffing and stock match its actual value before shifting more resource to Saturday.

ranked.limitation: Revenue per visit on a given weekday reflects who chose to come that day, not what that day itself does to spending.

ranked.pattern: Only 62.0% of revenue is classified to a category and only 55.0% of 8 active customers have a resolved age and gender — every category, cohort and mix finding below is drawn from that fraction.

comparison.detail: classified revenue coverage 6200 bps against 9000 bps, and demographic coverage 55.0% against 50.0%

impact.reason: a coverage defect has no revenue figure of its own; what it does is put an error bar on every figure above it

action.who: the owner, once, then front desk on an ongoing basis
action.what: Map every service and product to a category in Settings, and capture date of birth and gender at the point a customer is created rather than retrospectively.

ranked.limitation: Coverage is not accuracy: fully classified revenue can still be classified wrongly.

good:
## Summary
Whale Boutique had one very large customer this month. Revenue was SGD 10,000.00, and Chen H. alone carried 85.0% of it.

## What went well
- 7 of 8 customers this month had already bought before, a returning-customer share of 87.5%.
- 100% of revenue came from identified customers.

## What needs attention
- Chen H. carried SGD 8,500.00, or 85.0% of all revenue. That concentration is a strength and a risk: losing this customer would hurt badly.
- 1 regular has not been seen in a while. One returned visit is worth SGD 20.00.

## Your customers
Chen H. is by far your largest customer, at 85.0% of revenue.

## Do these three things next
1. Send one win-back message to the 1 at-risk regular this week. SGD 20.00 / 1 customer = SGD 20.00 each.
2. Build a second relationship with another customer so Chen H. is not the only large account.
3. Check in personally with Chen H. next month to keep the relationship strong.
